_comment: The palace worktree symlink manifest — the single source of truth for what a new git worktree must borrow from the canonical main worktree. A fresh worktree contains only TRACKED files; everything gitignored (venvs, model weights, node_modules, secrets) is absent and must be symlinked back to the main worktree that owns it. Read by _ops/worktree/new-worktree.mjs. See SKILL.md for the process + rationale.
owner_note: All symlinks point at the CANONICAL main worktree (git rev-parse --show-toplevel of the primary checkout). That one install is the owner; every other worktree borrows it. If the main worktree's path moves, the links break — re-run with the new owner.

auto_mirror._comment: Dependency CLASSES mirrored by DISCOVERY, not enumeration — so npm-workspace node_modules (one per package, at any depth) are all symlinked automatically, with zero manifest upkeep as packages are added. new-worktree.mjs runs `git -C <owner> ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory`, keeps every fully-ignored dir whose basename is in by_basename, and symlinks each at its relative path. `--directory` collapses an already-ignored tree (e.g. _tools/) to one entry, so its internal node_modules are never listed and never double-linked. This replaced the hand-listed `_ops/stigmergy/app/node_modules` link (2026-06-17), which missed the workspace-root + orchestrator + trickster-auto node_modules and broke vitest in fresh stigmergy worktrees.
auto_mirror.caveat: A symlinked node_modules preserves the install's OWN relative links — the npm-workspace link `@stigmergy/core -> ../../core` resolves, through the mirror, to the OWNER's core, not the worktree's. Harmless for running/testing (core is read-only and identical); only matters if a session edits a workspace package's source INSIDE a worktree and expects its own copy under test. For that, run `npm install` in the worktree instead.

links.why: ComfyUI app + its venv + ~13 GB of model weights (SDXL, xinsir ControlNets), plus stable-audio. Every Shop GPU/render job and all BLUELINE local rendering needs it. Not cheaply regenerable — re-downloading the weights is the whole cost. Rebuild recipe if ever needed: Shop/ComfyUI/ComfyUI — local-install.md.
Per-Specialist Python venvs (Kokoro, Whisper, …) live in .venvs/<specialist>/. Symlink to skip rebuilding each.

RunPod API key + endpoint id (gitignored secret). Needed to dispatch cloud renders. The parent 'RunPod Images/studio/' is tracked and already present in the worktree — only this file is missing, so symlink the FILE, not the dir. Never commit it.

links.regenerable: re-approve permissions in the new worktree
links.why: Local permission allowlists + settings. Symlink to inherit your already-approved commands instead of re-approving from scratch.

never_symlink: _ops/stigmergy/.actuator/  ·  .actuator-steward/  ·  .actuator-companion/ — per-process runtime pid/log + transcripts. Sharing these CROSS-WIRES running stewards across worktrees. Must stay per-worktree.
__pycache__/ · _manim_media/ · **/.remotion/ · .vite/ · **/_*.mp4 · **/_*.png · *.asd — regenerable caches; let them rebuild from source in the worktree.

memory.why: Auto-memory (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/) is keyed to the worktree's ABSOLUTE PATH, not the repo. A worktree at a new path gets a fresh, empty memory — you lose all accumulated palace memories (how Loudon works, the git hazards, etc.). CLAUDE.md still loads (it's tracked in the repo); only the auto-memory is path-keyed.
memory.fix: Symlink the new worktree's memory/ dir to the canonical one. The new slug is the worktree's absolute path with every '/' replaced by '-'. new-worktree.mjs prints the exact ready-to-run command for the worktree it creates (run with --memory to apply it automatically).
memory.caveat: Outside the repo (touches ~/.claude). Sharing memory means writes from either worktree land in the same files — intended for continuity, but be aware it is shared state.
